stem.text: An open-top storage bin is made from a rectangular sheet of steel 50 inches by 80 inches by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. Find the largest possible volume of the storage bin, in cubic inches.

worked_solution.text: The storage bin has height x and a base \( 50 - 2 x \) by \( 80 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(50 - 2 x\right)\left(80 - 2 x\right) \).
The cut must be positive and less than half the sheet, so the domain is \( 0 < x < 25 \).
\( V'(x) = 4 \left(x - 10\right) \left(3 x - 100\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 10 \) and \( x = \frac{100}{3} \); only \( x = 10 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
\( V'(x) \) is positive for \( 0 < x < 10 \) and negative for \( 10 < x < 25 \), and this is the only critical point in the domain, so V has its absolute maximum there.
worked_solution.rule_named: first derivative test for an absolute extremum

worked_solution.text: The largest volume is \( V(10) = 10\left(30\right)\left(60\right) = 18000 \) cubic inches.
